title: Cryo-Expansion Microscopy of C. elegans and Tardigrades
author: Matthew Lycas
materials: Degas both cryoprotectant solutions prior to use by placing them following mixing in a cell media sterilization flask connected to a vacuum. Run the vacuum until no more bubbles emerge from the solution
Monitor specimen release under the dissectionmicroscope:
For NHS ester total protein staining:
Re-expand gel in deionized water for 1 hour.
Re-expand in deionized water until fully expanded.

steps.title: Collect C. elegans specimens
steps.instruction: Transfer C. elegans from culture plates into a well of a 9‑well borosilicate spot plate using a worm pick or a P200 pipette; pool enough animals for multiple high‑pressure freezing (HPF) runs.

steps.title: Collect tardigrades from moss
steps.instruction: Collect moss from tree bark, place it in a 60 mm Petri dish, add deionized water until the moss is barely submerged, and incubate at room temperature for 45 min to allow tardigrades to egress into the water film.

steps.title: Isolate tardigrades
steps.instruction: Under a stereodissection microscope, locate individual tardigrades in the water film and pick them with a P200 pipette, transferring each organism to a separate well of the 9‑well spot plate.

steps.title: Add cryoprotectant
steps.instruction: In a separate well of the spot plate add 1 mL of the appropriate cryoprotectant: 20 % fetal bovine serum (FBS) in deionized water for tardigrades, or 20 % dextran in 0.1 M phosphate buffer (PB) for C. elegans.

steps.title: Pre‑cool HPF freezer
steps.instruction: Fill the internal dewar of the Leica EM ICE high‑pressure freezer with liquid nitrogen (LN₂) from a large storage dewar, allow the machine to equilibrate (~20 min), then fill the sample‑collection dewar with LN₂ and insert it into the freezer chamber before starting any runs.

steps.title: Mark and coat planchets
steps.instruction: Mark the shallow (0.1 mm) face of all Type A planchets with a permanent marker; immerse the flat face of each Type B planchet in anhydrous hexadecane, blot briefly, and place on a post‑it note to leave a thin, even film.

steps.title: Load specimens onto planchet
steps.instruction: Assemble the loading cartridge: place a Type A planchet into the cartridge holder with the 0.2 mm depression facing upward. Using a P2 pipette set to 2 µL, quickly dispense the maximum number of specimens from the cryoprotectant well into the depression.

steps.title: Sandwich and freeze sample
steps.instruction: Seat the hexadecane‑coated flat face of the Type B planchet on top of the Type A planchet to sandwich the sample, close the loading lever, and initiate the HPF run (≈2 000 bar, milliseconds).

steps.title: Collect frozen planchet assembly
steps.instruction: Eject the frozen planchet assembly and deposit it into the LN₂‑filled collection reservoir inside the HPF machine.

steps.title: Repeat HPF runs
steps.instruction: Perform one blank (empty) run at the start of the session to purge the system, then repeat the specimen‑loading and freezing steps for a total of 10 HPF runs.

steps.title: Retrieve planchets under LN₂
steps.instruction: While maintaining LN₂, remove the planchet assemblies from the collection dewar, identify each Type A planchet by the permanent mark on its 0.1 mm face, and separate the two planchets under cryogenic conditions.

steps.title: Prepare frozen acetone block
steps.instruction: Add 50 mL anhydrous acetone to an 80 mL plastic beaker, cover with aluminum foil, and submerge the beaker in an LN₂ bath until the acetone freezes solid and the beaker reaches LN₂ temperature (several minutes).

steps.title: Transfer planchets onto acetone
steps.instruction: Under LN₂ vapor, bring the planchet assemblies (in a plastic carrier) into LN₂, remove the foil from the frozen acetone block, and using fine forceps place each planchet onto the surface of the frozen acetone. Re‑cover the beaker with foil.

steps.title: Cold acetone substitution
steps.instruction: Place the covered beaker in a –80 °C freezer and store for 7 days; during this time acetone slowly permeates the sample, replacing vitreous water while preserving ultrastructure.

steps.title: Warm to room temperature
steps.instruction: Remove the beaker from the –80 °C freezer and allow it to warm to room temperature on the benchtop for 8 hours.

steps.title: Rehydrate through ethanol series
steps.instruction: In a 6‑well tissue‑culture plate prepare a rehydration series (2 mL per well): 100 % ethanol (×2), 95 % ethanol (×2), 75 % ethanol, 50 % ethanol, 25 % ethanol, then 1× PBS. Transfer each planchet assembly sequentially through the ethanol steps and finally into PBS, incubating 5–10 min per step.

steps.title: Extract specimens after rehydration
steps.instruction: For C. elegans, animals detach around the 50 % ethanol step and become suspended in PBS; for tardigrades, FBS forms a gel that must be manually broken with fine forceps under a dissection microscope after the PBS wash to release the organisms.

steps.title: Wash in NaHCO₃
steps.instruction: Wash specimens twice in 0.1 M NaHCO₃ using the spot plate (2 × 5 min).

steps.title: GMA cross‑linking
steps.instruction: Incubate specimens in 0.1 % (v/v) glycidyl methacrylate (GMA) prepared in 0.1 M NaHCO₃, shaking overnight at room temperature to covalently anchor proteins to the future expansion gel.

steps.title: PBS wash post‑GMA
steps.instruction: Wash specimens three times in 1× PBS (5 min each).

steps.title: Infiltrate non‑activated monomer
steps.instruction: Transfer specimens to a non‑activated monomer solution containing 23 % (w/v) sodium acrylate, 10 % (w/v) acrylamide, 0.1 % (w/v) Bis‑acrylamide in 1× PBS; incubate overnight at 4 °C with gentle agitation.

steps.title: Prepare gelation chamber
steps.instruction: On a clean glass slide place two layers of double‑sided adhesive tape (≈200 µm total thickness) parallel to each other to form walls; this creates a spacer chamber for gelation.

steps.title: Activate monomer solution
steps.instruction: Add TEMED and ammonium persulfate (APS) to fresh cold non‑activated monomer solution to final concentrations of 0.25 % each; mix gently by pipetting.

steps.title: Embed sample in gel
steps.instruction: Pipette the activated monomer solution onto the specimens, mix briefly by up‑and‑down pipetting, then transfer the specimen + solution into the tape‑spaced chamber on the glass slide; gently place a coverslip on top.

steps.title: Gelation incubation
steps.instruction: Seal the chamber in a humidified container (plastic box with damp tissue) and incubate at 37 °C for 1 hour to polymerize the gel.

steps.title: Extract gel piece
steps.instruction: After polymerization, carefully disassemble the chamber and cut out the gel piece containing the embedded specimen with a clean razor blade or scalpel.

steps.title: Enzymatic digestion
steps.instruction: Transfer the gel piece to enzymatic disruption buffer composed of 1 mg/mL collagenase Type IV, 1 mg/mL chitinase, 500 mM NaCl, 50 mM CaCl₂ in Tris‑HCl pH 7.0; incubate overnight at 37 °C with shaking (100 RPM).

steps.title: SDS denaturation
steps.instruction: Move the gel piece to SDS denaturation solution (200 mM SDS, 200 mM NaCl, 50 mM Tris, pH 9.0) and incubate at 95 °C for 2 hours.

steps.title: Expand and wash gel
steps.instruction: Wash the gel piece 2–3 times in deionized water to allow expansion and remove SDS; then equilibrate briefly in PBS until the size change stops.

steps.title: NHS‑ester staining
steps.instruction: Incubate the expanded gel in 20 µM NHS‑ester dye prepared in PBS for 2 hours at room temperature with gentle agitation.

steps.title: Re‑expand and buffer equilibration
steps.instruction: Perform three water exchanges (deionized water) to re‑expand the gel, then equilibrate in PBS containing 3 % BSA and 0.1 % sodium azide.

steps.title: Primary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the gel in primary antibody diluted 1:100 in PBS + 3 % BSA + 0.1 % sodium azide, overnight at 37 °C (azide prevents bacterial growth).

steps.title: Wash after primary
steps.instruction: Wash three times in PBS (5 min each).

steps.title: Secondary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the gel in secondary antibody at 5 µg/mL in PBS + 3 % BSA + 0.1 % sodium azide, overnight at 37 °C.

steps.title: Wash after secondary
steps.instruction: Wash two times in PBS (5 min each).

steps.title: Optional PFA post‑fixation
steps.instruction: Post‑fix the gel in 6 % paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS for 30 min at room temperature; omit this step if subsequent sequential labeling is planned.

steps.title: SYBR Gold nuclear stain
steps.instruction: Incubate the gel in 1:10 000 SYBR Gold solution prepared in deionized water for 10 min, then wash 2–3 times with deionized water to remove excess stain.

steps.title: Select imaging face
steps.instruction: Place the expanded gel on an uncoated glass‑bottom MatTek dish and examine with a wide‑field fluorescence microscope (water‑immersion objective) to locate the gel face that contains the most specimens closest to the coverslip surface.

steps.title: Mount gel on PDL coverslip
steps.instruction: Place the gel flat, specimen‑rich face down onto a poly‑D‑lysine‑coated 25 mm round coverslip; blot excess water with a Kimwipe or lint‑free tissue (do not let the gel dry).

steps.title: Press and re‑equilibrate
steps.instruction: Gently press the gel against the coverslip using the flat of a clean fine‑bristled paintbrush, then submerge the coverslip and gel in deionized water in a well of a 6‑well plate for ~30 min to re‑equilibrate.

steps.title: Mount for imaging
steps.instruction: Insert the PDL‑coated coverslip with adherent gel into a coverslip holder, fill the holder with the same deionized water used for storage as immersion medium, and image using either a Nikon NSPARC array detector system or a Yokogawa CSU‑W1 spinning‑disk confocal. Acquire channels for NHS‑ester (total protein), antibody (specific targets), and SYBR Gold (DNA).

steps.title: Store planchets cryogenically
steps.instruction: Transfer all planchets to a cryogenic storage vessel and transport to the laboratory immersed in liquid nitrogen.
